## Surprises and Discoveries

- V28's V27 transform was textually deterministic but not historically
  closed: unqualified `CONTRACTS` and `CONTRACT_HASHES` resolved to the active
  V28 objects. Only policy/toolchain and trusted-context differed, adding 60
  bytes while leaving the other three contract hashes unchanged. A final
  derived-driver hash gate caught the error before `mkdir`; version-scoped
  positive and exact-mutation-negative fixtures now make the cause local.

- V26's external receipt and frozen closure carried identical values but not
  identical Python container types. JSON decoding converted exactly 13
  `(size, sha256)` tuples to lists. Raw object equality therefore rejected
  valid canonical JSON before root creation; normalization removes only that
  representation difference and still rejects any changed value.

- Root-only success does not prove that the transported driver will accept the
  external receipt it just sealed. V19's preparation source generated the
  receipt from current V19 contracts, but its deterministic driver transform
  retained older `CONTROLLER_CONTRACT_HASHES` values. Root self-check did not
  compare those two independently immutable objects. Post-root inspection did,
  finding exact mismatches only in `policy_toolchain` and `trusted_context`.
- Independent historical/current document generations are structurally
  preserved in V19, but that does not bypass the contradiction. The historical
  receipt is validated first, current execute documents are validated later by
  `read_only_gates`, and both precede allocation. Changing current document
  hashes cannot make the earlier semantic receipt comparison pass.

- `read_regular` deliberately returns a seven-key dictionary, not
  `os.stat_result`; V18's first bad `info.st_mode` access merely masked later
  bad `info.st_uid` and `reread_info.st_uid` accesses. A one-line repair would
  therefore have produced a second stopped successor. The safe correction
  fixes all dataflow-equivalent uses and leaves the shared identity schema
  unchanged.
- Ownership cannot be inferred from a dictionary that intentionally omits uid.
  V19 reopens the exact dictionary-bound inode with `O_NOFOLLOW`, checks uid
  and mode on the descriptor, and correlates a final `lstat`; receipts still
  expose only the established identity schema.

- Execute-only reachability does not exempt dormant Python string constants
  from an all-source exact-token policy. V17 correctly removed auth but its
  inherited dormant writer self-test/finalize code retained two exact writer
  phase constants, so the runtime validator stopped before allocation. V18
  keeps their semantics via concatenated literals and validates the final
  derived bytes with the same AST rule plus failure-reproducing fixtures.
- Expanding the sealed V17 receipt tuple gives 38 names, not the 37 asserted
  by a dormant legacy self-check helper. The sole command surface is
  execute-only and does not reach that helper; live sealing uses the 38-name
  tuple. The frozen boundary therefore records both the executable count and
  the unreachable stale fixture instead of hiding either.

- The V17 root checkpoint confirms the active/full-vocabulary correction
  statically and at root self-check, but root success alone cannot authorize
  allocation. Current post-root documents remain a distinct execute-time
  generation and must be closed and bound in the later argv.

- A historical phase vocabulary is not an executable requirement set. Reusing
  the vocabulary as the active set made a deliberately removed auth capability
  mandatory. V17 makes the subset relation explicit and rejects any inactive
  current-version phase literal.

- A cryptographically sealed producer receipt is not proof of external
  acceptance when the producer chose the verdict string. Both V13 Planners
  independently found the same provenance gap: the candidate could inspect
  final bindings and trusted context, but could not distinguish
  `READY_FOR_CONTROLLER_REVIEW` / `CONTROLLER_BOUND_FINAL` from self-asserted
  authority. The correction is an externally constructed pre-root receipt,
  not a more emphatic driver-generated label.
- Binding a future unpredictable suffix and run does not require circular
  acceptance. The controller accepts the closed driver, seed, exact
  predecessor set, one-shot allocation/init rules, trusted-context transport,
  policy/toolchain expectations, and formal-dispatch contract before root
  creation. Later driver receipts prove which single allowed realization
  occurred; they never create controller authority.
- The acceptance receipt must live outside the policy snapshot input set.
  Transporting its exact bytes to `.loop/trusted/` makes it visible to fresh
  roles while avoiding a self-referential policy digest. Its hash is carried
  by final bindings and its authority comes solely from pre-root controller
  acceptance.
- The successful opaque handoff needs no credential-derived proof in the
  execution plan. A 262-byte eight-field receipt can establish exclusive-copy
  success, private destination mode/ownership, and supported authenticated
  status while revealing no auth bytes or auth-file metadata. Formal preflight
  therefore trusts only that accepted non-secret receipt and must not reopen or
  revalidate either authentication file.
- The formal outer environment remains the established seven-name map rather
  than the eight-name handoff map. `HOME` selects the already authenticated
  private candidate home; checked-in `safe_child_env()` continues stripping
  credential-bearing variables from every role. Authentication is discovered
  by the pinned Codex client through private HOME, not forwarded through argv
  or environment.
- The credential-free V13 path completed in 215.915482 wrapper seconds and
  sealed a pristine candidate/run without ever reaching the auth routines.
  This confirms that authentication is a later authority boundary rather than
  a materialization, setup, readiness, doctor, or init prerequisite.
- The auth handoff is intentionally a direct driver call, not a bounded-wrapper
  call. The driver writes one minimal no-replace receipt itself, while the
  sensitive copy and the fixed login-status child's stdout/stderr never enter
  wrapper output, receipt output, hashes, manifests, or diagnostics.
- The sealed `auth-handoff` schema has 35 driver tokens and therefore 37 full
  Python argv strings. With `/usr/bin/env`, `-i`, and the exact eight-name
  private environment, the always-single-quoted shell vector has 47 tokens;
  reusing the 17-token candidate-recovery wrapper envelope would invoke the
  wrong authority surface.
- The sealed V13 root index carries one root-prepare argv hash rather than the
  V11/V12 transport/self-check/finalize triple. Consequently the immutable
  driver intentionally narrows candidate recovery to a 23-token subcommand
  shape (25 strings including pinned Python and driver), with
  `--expected-root-prepare-argv-json-sha256` binding the accepted root-only
  provenance. Reusing the older 29-string schema would be a mismatch, not a
  compatible alias.
- The explicit operator authorization changes the supported recovery from a
  hypothetical access-token login to an opaque copy of the already
  authenticated file-backed Codex state. Official Codex documentation permits
  copying `auth.json` to another machine and identifies the default path as
  `~/.codex/auth.json`; it also warns that the file is password-equivalent.
  That makes content inspection, hashing, diffing, receipt inclusion, and
  manifesting categorically inappropriate. V13 therefore validates only
  source safety internally, writes one no-replace private destination, and
  exposes only boolean/mode/owner/status outcomes.
- The accepted private state may instead be absent or unavailable because
  Codex can use an OS credential store. V13 does not probe that fact during
  design and has no export/fallback path. A later handoff stops with a fixed
  sanitized code before any role if the exact default file source cannot be
  opened safely.
- The one authorized V12 formal dispatch reached only the fresh Planner and
  then failed authentication before a session or schema artifact existed.
  The bounded redacted event log shows repeated WebSocket 401 responses,
  fallback to HTTPS Responses, and the same 401 outcome with the sanitized
  diagnostic `Missing [REDACTED] [REDACTED] in header`. This is not a Planner
  reasoning failure or product-code failure. The outer `env -i` contract had
  no credential, candidate-private HOME contained the reviewed profiles but
  no authorized login state, and `safe_child_env()` correctly removes
  credential-bearing environment variables before launching every role.

- Credential isolation and non-interactive authentication are separate
  contracts. Preserving the current environment filter prevents a secret from
  reaching model-controlled shell commands. Official OpenAI documentation
  describes `codex login --with-access-token` with the token supplied on
  stdin as the persistent-login alternative to a `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN`
  environment variable. Because the latter is deliberately removed by the
  current filter, the smallest no-control-plane-change recovery is a private
  login bootstrap in a fresh successor HOME. It still requires new operator
  authority, eligibility for the chosen credential kind, a bounded redacted
  launcher, and an explicit retention/revocation policy; none is inferred
  from standing recovery authority.

- M3S-v10 failed because raw substring matching treated the valid active token
  `M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_V10` as if it contained a standalone predecessor
  `M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_V1`. The immutable input and active phase were
  correct; the validator's version-token model was not. V11 parses Python
  string literals and compares complete tokens, so V1, V10, and V11 remain
  distinct while an exact standalone predecessor phase still fails closed.

- M3S-v9 failed on a correct immutable document because its generic 4 MiB
  buffered-read bound was reused for the growing Living ExecPlan. The accepted
  plan was 4,194,810 bytes—exactly 506 bytes over 4,194,304—and the failing
  read was inside the V8 procedural-stop validator. Hash streaming, receipt
  bounds, and retained evidence were not the defect. V10 therefore introduces
  a plan-specific 8 MiB bound instead of weakening unrelated file limits.

- The first V9 static closure found that envelope-v5 still bound the immutable
  V8 writer/driver identities even though its root, markers, and orchestrator
  were V9. No source ran and no root existed. The V9-only envelope constants
  now bind the extracted V9 writer and driver, and the full historical-source,
  Ruff, structural, round-trip, and malicious-fixture checks were repeated.

- M3S-v8 contained correct frozen bytes but its first combined validation
  helper used `exec(compile(...), {})`, evaluating top-level definitions even
  though no main guard or side effect fired. That violates the stronger
  compile-without-execution boundary. V9 validation therefore permits only raw
  extraction, `ast.parse`, compile-only checks, structural AST inspection, and
  Ruff over stdin; it never imports or evaluates an embedded range.

- M3S-v7 authenticated the correct blocked `state.json` bytes but asserted one
  semantic field incorrectly: `code_cycle` is 1, not 0. The same immutable
  object cross-correlates cycle 1, the recorded Coder session, and exactly one
  Planner plus one Coder artifact. A hash check alone did not make a mismatched
  semantic assertion true; V8 binds both the byte identity and exact parsed
  shape.

- M3S-v6 failed on a correct path with an incorrect expected digest: the
  6,282,115-byte `final-attempt-manifest.jsonl` is a serialized manifest whose
  own SHA-256 is a0f211b6..., while c5d16be1... describes the later completed
  attempt tree. The final index and outer result already preserve both values
  independently; the defect was V6's overloaded `M2_ATTEMPT_SHA` name/value,
  not evidence drift.

- **2026-10-09 — Immutable V3 has five shared receipt-tuple uses, not four.**
  V5 stopped before writer self-test and finalization because its exact
  retained-evidence assertion was wrong. V6 requires five, validates the exact
  V5 receipt/failure/absence shape, and treats V5 only as a consumed immutable
  predecessor.

- **2026-10-09 — The accepted direct-argv source exceeded the execution
  tool's interface.** The tool accepts one shell command string, not an argv
  array. Refusing ad hoc quoting preserved the boundary and left V5 absent.
  The corrected envelope uses one reviewable zsh grammar rather than treating
  shell text as a general command language.

- **2026-10-09 — Exact source transport necessarily contains LF bytes.** The
  accepted 42,768-byte `-c` element has exactly 1,077 LFs and 30 single quotes.
  A no-control-byte rule was therefore impossible until the controller allowed
  those LFs only inside the exact source token. Envelope-v1 rejects LF in all
  other tokens and reconstructs the accepted source byte-for-byte.

- **2026-10-09 — AST attribute names are not direct builtin calls.** The v2
  scanner assigned both `ast.Name` and `ast.Attribute` callees to `name`, then
  rejected every `compile` string. Its own `re.compile` therefore made the
  launcher deterministically self-reject before root creation. V3 applies the
  direct-builtin denylist only to `ast.Name`, treats qualified OS/subprocess
  surfaces separately, and proves the exact predicate against its full source.

- **2026-10-09 — A prose-only pinned-Python requirement did not identify the
  bytes of the local launcher.** The zero-write proof incorrectly used host
  `python3` and heredoc/stdin source even though the frozen V5 contract
  prohibited both. Controller interruption preserved root absence. The
  correction freezes the launcher itself, binds its literal `-c` argv, and
  makes prohibited-mechanism fixtures part of the pre-root proof.

- **2026-10-09 — Command construction is part of the one-shot mutation
  boundary.** The accepted V4 source never ran: after the no-replace root was
  created, the surrounding JavaScript context attempted to use unavailable
  `TextEncoder` and stopped before wrapper invocation. V5 therefore makes
  canonical argv/UTF-8 construction a pinned-Python/POSIX-only read-only
  preflight that must pass before `mkdir`; JavaScript runtimes and
  `TextEncoder` are outside the execution contract. The one occurrence in
  V5 source is only the immutable V4 failure string.

- **2026-10-09 — Historical sealed receipt schemas are not future execution
  schemas.** M3S-v3 compiled and fixed the prior ownership shape, but its
  self-check applied a 37-name successor tuple to V5/V7 stopped candidates.
  Their directories are internally exact: each is the 27 files authenticated
  by its final receipt index plus that index. The mismatch was in the new
  validator, not the retained evidence. V4 gives the historical 28-name and
  future 37-name domains distinct constants, validators, and misuse fixtures.

- M3S-v2 failed on a data-shape mismatch, not filesystem drift: the generic
  directory record intentionally had no owner field, while the validator
  indexed `uid`. The private helper already proves owner/mode/no-follow and
  exposes `owner_uid`; V3 centralizes retained-root checks on that contract
  and fixtures the exact generic/private shapes so the mismatch is caught
  before future root authority.

- **2026-10-09 — A source scanner can self-trigger on its own denylist literals.** M3S-v1 embedded contiguous `M3S_V2_` and `M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_V2` bytes once each inside the tuple used to forbid those bytes. Transport therefore passed, but self-check deterministically raised `RuntimeError: forbidden successor source token` before writer-self-test or finalize. V2 constructs predecessor/future comparison tokens from split fragments and proves positive V2 plus negative stale-V1/future-V3 fixtures without embedding future tokens contiguously.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: decimal version prefixes make V1 a substring of V10 and V11.
  Mitigation: parse complete Python string constants and compare exact phase
  tokens against generated active, predecessor, and future sets; fixtures
  require V1/V10/V11 distinction and rejection of standalone exact V1.

- Risk: the Living ExecPlan grows past the plan-specific read ceiling or a new
  call bypasses it. Mitigation: fail before mutation unless the closed plan is
  no larger than 8,388,608 bytes; accept the exact boundary and reject
  boundary-plus-one; structurally require the sole underlying PLAN-buffering
  call to name `LIVING_PLAN_MAX_BYTES`; preserve all other default bounds.

- Risk: another generic "attempt" field could silently exchange a manifest
  file identity and a completed-tree summary. Mitigation: V8 has separately
  named size/hash/count constants, validates the manifest file directly, and
  requires exact parsed final-index/outer-result agreement before root
  creation or successor allocation.
- Risk: a root-only retry could overwrite forensic evidence. Mitigation: V6 is
  immutable/consumed, V7 is separately immutable/consumed, and V8 is a
  distinct absent O_EXCL namespace with a single root budget and retain-on-stop
  semantics.

- A copied historical evidence assertion can stop a later root self-check even
  when the predecessor is unchanged. V6 binds immutable V3's exact five-use
  count and the complete retained V5 shape, with positive and negative
  fixtures, before any future root creation.
- A command-tool string can diverge from a reviewed argv. Envelope-v2 permits
  only the frozen non-login zsh `exec`/`env -i` grammar, exact token vector,
  source-token-only LF exception, canonical round trip, and malicious-fixture
  rejection; no shell construction is authorized by this checkpoint.

- Risk: a future successor receipt tuple is reused for immutable historical
  attempts. Mitigation: V4 freezes disjoint named contracts, authenticates
  each historical directory against its own sealed final index, fixtures set
  misuse, and traverses every validator invoked before finalization.

- Risk: a validator can compile yet index a field absent from the producer's
  identity schema. Mitigation: V3 requires exact key sets, uses
  `owner_uid` only through the private ownership-enforcing helper, rejects
  legacy `uid` fixtures, and correlates both historical stopped roots before
  any future root can finalize.

| A version scanner rejects its own denylist | V2 future/stale comparison tokens are assembled from split fragments, active phases remain explicit, and self-check fixtures require active-V2 acceptance plus stale-V1/future-V3 rejection. |
| A stopped M3S root is reused or silently repaired | V1 is validated as an exact immutable predecessor with consumed budget and absent finalization artifacts. V2 has a distinct absent root and separate literal authority. |
| V2 source freeze is mistaken for runtime authority | This task edits only the two documents. Controller must accept closed documents, raw sources, static evidence, and acyclic command hashes before any root-only mutation; execute needs a later distinct accepted-index authority. |

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| A command-string tool turns the accepted argv into general shell syntax | Envelope-v1 admits only literal `exec`, 42 canonical single-quoted tokens, single spaces, and one final `</dev/null`; its parser must reconstruct the controller-accepted vector exactly. Every expansion, substitution, operator, extra command/redirection, alternate transport, or altered source fails. |
| Source newlines are mistaken for shell separators | Permit exactly 1,077 LF bytes only while parsing token 12 inside its single-quote state, require the exact source hash and quote count, and reject LF everywhere else. |
| A compliant driver is launched by noncompliant or self-rejecting orchestration | Bind the complete orchestration-v3 bytes and 32-string literal `-c` argv after document closure. The exact call-policy self-fixture must report zero violations while negative fixtures reject direct dynamic builtins and unsafe OS/subprocess surfaces. Preflight retains the pinned Python/environment/CWD and prohibited-mechanism gates and constructs every later phase array before root creation. |
| The command-construction layer consumes a fresh root before proving it can encode the frozen argv | V5 requires a zero-write pinned-Python/POSIX UTF-8 and canonical-JSON round-trip before `mkdir`; JavaScript, `TextEncoder`, shell evaluation, generated source, and post-root reconstruction are forbidden. Any preflight mismatch leaves the root absent and budget unconsumed. |
| A permission-layer rejection is mistaken for an executed root attempt | Require post-rejection root absence and unchanged inventory/budgets. Continue only after explicit access-mode authority in the same trusted Main session and a complete repeated pre-root gate; never bypass through an alternate path. |
| Authorized current suffix is mistaken for predecessor drift | Freeze the exact fifteen-name predecessor set, record the sole current directory identity at `mktemp`, require exact set equality to predecessors plus current, validate those classes separately, and self-test rejection of every missing/substituted/extra case. |
| Candidate doctor resolves profiles from a credential-free private HOME rather than the validated operator home | V4 stages only the five exact reviewed profile bytes into a new private `.codex`, with no config/credential/unrelated copy, then binds source/destination identities and fsync evidence. |
| A poll failure skips termination, or receipt presence falsely seals a possibly live doctor child | V4 records poll failure but continues recorded-pid TERM→KILL; only an observed return code proves termination. Before indexing, it cross-validates doctor capture/validation identities and lifecycle fields. Spawn failure with no child may seal; spawned/unknown `still-live`, `indeterminate`, or otherwise unproven termination adds `doctor-child-termination-unproven` and forces incomplete sealing. |
| External retained base is outside default sandbox writes | Use only the exact operator-authorized base; stop if managed execution denies it or the base is unsafe. |
| Original changes during candidate work | Compare every B2 preimage immediately before CAS; third-value drift stops. |
| Protected data enters candidate | Permit only the two hash-bound tracked B2 data scaffolds, overlay only the frozen 71 ordinary-untracked paths, require every other data/input record absent, and independently prove all 83 excluded paths absent. |
| Candidate dependencies escape or break by symlink | Require strict resolution of every link inside the candidate, the exact absolute managed-Python alias, real local roots, and checked-in readiness/safe-tree checks. |
| Pinned `uv` drifts or resolves through the wrong path | Rehash the non-symlink absolute executable and receipts before use; require `UV_REL` to resolve exactly to it; stop on any mismatch and forbid substitution. |
| Setup imports credentials or writes outside the new candidate | Use a private HOME/TMPDIR and `env -i`; bind only the reviewed PATH, Make `UV`, relative cache, and quoted absolute candidate install root; stop on any credential demand or external root. |
| Make/uv mishandles the `Application Support` path | Require the raw and normalized immutable-seed dry-run hashes, parsed shell tokens, candidate-local repetition, and the candidate-specific quoted absolute install root; strict-resolve the resulting alias before readiness. |
| Outer wrapper selects an incompatible or drifting Python | Use only the absolute Python 3.12 link and resolved target frozen above; revalidate version/arch/hash/imports under `env -i`; never fall back to `/usr/bin/python3` or bypass `run_bounded`. |
| Receipt-local wrapper or proof bytes change between review and execution | Candidate eleven stopped when its post-allocation probe differed from the accepted bytes. Candidate twelve may use only a fully plan-frozen external driver and immutable wrapper; the driver verifies its own O_NOFOLLOW identity before mutation, remains the same live process across `mktemp`, and rechecks the same inode/bytes immediately afterward. |
| M2B driver transport lacks a durable generic writer | No current loop CLI or OS utility satisfies the contract. Use only the 9,513-byte source frozen here as the exact Python `-c` transport exception, create the fixed root with exact direct `mkdir` argv, and require the driver to validate/fsync wrapper receipts before final indexing. |
| Final document and command hashes form a self-reference | Freeze source/schema only in documents. The controller computes full closed-document and exact canonical argv-JSON hashes in memory and binds them in later authorization; never write those literals back into the same documents, STATUS, a new manifest, or a projection-hash scheme. |
| M2B preparation or its stopped execute result is confused with candidate authority | M2B is complete and its one-shot budget consumed; preserve its fixed root, four preparation receipts, and one stopped execution result immutably. Candidate twelve never reached `mktemp`, and neither the accepted M2B verdict nor the unused suffix condition authorizes a retry or candidate. |
| Manifest data match but serialization is noncanonical | Emit only frozen `tracked` and `ordinary-untracked` class tokens; compare raw canonical source/candidate bytes and SHA before setup; retain and stop without normalization or repair. |
| Restricted sandbox reports a false code-sign failure | Rehash all pinned payloads, then run the exact sealed deep/strict `codesign` verification outside that restriction; any sealed-command failure remains a hard stop. |
| Current docs are mistaken for frozen B2 source | Source only from immutable `candidate.OlsWg1/repo`; verify the current-original comparison and all 2,322 B2 records before setup. |
| Profile installation overwrites or broadens user Codex state | The retained post-install receipt already proves exactly five reviewed additions, exact mode/hash, and unchanged other-40 metadata at the install boundary. Preserve those files/receipts; no replay or widening is allowed. |
| Live Codex runtime metadata is mistaken for immutable configuration | Accept only the sealed, command-correlated five-file installer delta, exact profiles/config, exact doctor READY, and LiveClip-owned repository/protected/attempt/tool identities. Do not use whole-home name/metadata equality or maintain a volatile-name allowlist; do not infer safety or provenance for unrelated runtime writes. |
| Static `config.toml` drifts after the accepted M2P boundary | Preserve the historical 1,473-byte/`32f2f367...` receipt; bind candidate twelve to the controller-correlated current mode/inode/timestamps/1,471-byte/`58676489...` identity; rely on the five independent role-profile hashes for role reasoning settings; stop on any further drift. No credential or unrelated value enters evidence. |
| A failing post-allocation gate also breaks its exception-path preservation check | Carry the accepted pre-allocation snapshot across `mktemp`; write preflight first; never rerun mutable gates while sealing; attempt each no-replace seal independently with bounded ordered errors; make the final wrapper result expose incomplete sealing and never claim permanent I/O recovery. |
| M2B state or finalize invocation admits an extra path/environment value | The completed preparation boundary required exact owned mode-`0700` root/home/tmp/receipts directories, exact phase receipt names, exact driver identity, absent reserved result, empty private home/tmp, and the exact credential-free finalize environment/argv hash. After execute, preserve exactly the same root plus its one consumed reserved result; any sixth receipt or other drift stops. |
| A byte-bound stdout artifact is captured through a merged stderr channel | Candidate twelve proved that `run_bounded` merges stderr into stdout, so a host `confstr()` warning changes the bytes presented to `git_bytes()` even while Git patch stdout is exact. Preserve both observed hashes and analyze channel separation read-only; do not strip warnings, change the frozen patch, rerun, or mutate the immutable driver/root without a reviewed amendment and explicit authority. |
| CoreFoundation temp lookup changes stderr across execution contexts | Accept only byte-empty stderr or the exact tool-specific frozen `confstr()` warning, keep stdout/argv/CWD/environment/bounds exact, and record `policy`, `variant`, observed size, and observed SHA in each selected evidence record. Reject every other byte identity; do not strip, regex-match, or broaden. |
| Candidate-specific absolute paths make a seed raw-output hash non-portable | The retained attempt proves the raw dry-run gate stopped before normalization. Preserve its bytes and receipts; design any correction read-only so normalized identity is checked at the correct boundary without accepting arbitrary output. Do not rerun Make, patch the retained driver, or allocate another suffix. |

def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise RuntimeError(message)


def sha(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def compact(value: object) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps(
        value,
        ensure_ascii=False,
        allow_nan=False,
        separators=(",", ":"),
        sort_keys=True,
    ).encode("utf-8")


def pretty(value: object) -> bytes:
    return (
        json.dumps(
            value,
            ensure_ascii=False,
            allow_nan=False,
            indent=2,
            sort_keys=True,
        )
        + "\n"
    ).encode("utf-8")


def argv_json(argv: list[str]) -> bytes:
    require(argv and all(isinstance(item, str) and item for item in argv), "invalid argv")
    return json.dumps(
        argv,
        ensure_ascii=False,
        allow_nan=False,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    ).encode("utf-8")


def read_regular(path: Path, maximum: int = GENERIC_MAX_BYTES) -> tuple[bytes, os.stat_result]:
    before = path.lstat()
    require(stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode) and not path.is_symlink(), "unsafe regular file")
    require(before.st_size <= maximum, "file exceeds read bound")
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    chunks: list[bytes] = []
    try:
        opened = os.fstat(fd)
        require(
            (opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino, opened.st_size)
            == (before.st_dev, before.st_ino, before.st_size),
            "opened identity mismatch",
        )
        while True:
            chunk = os.read(fd, 1024 * 1024)
            if not chunk:
                break
            chunks.append(chunk)
        final = os.fstat(fd)
        require(
            (final.st_dev, final.st_ino, final.st_size)
            == (opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino, opened.st_size),
            "read identity changed",
        )
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    payload = b"".join(chunks)
    require(len(payload) == before.st_size, "short read")
    return payload, before


def identity(path: Path, size: int, digest: str, mode: int | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    payload, info = read_regular(path)
    require(len(payload) == size and sha(payload) == digest, "file identity mismatch")
    if mode is not None:
        require(stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) == mode, "file mode mismatch")
    return {"mode": f"{stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode):04o}", "sha256": digest, "size": size}


def private_directory(path: Path, names: set[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    info = path.lstat()
    require(
        stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode)
        and not path.is_symlink()
        and info.st_uid == CURRENT_UID
        and stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) == 0o700,
        "private directory mismatch",
    )
    observed = set(os.listdir(path))
    if names is not None:
        require(observed == names, "private directory entries mismatch")
    return {"mode": "0700", "owner_uid": info.st_uid}


def extract_once(payload: bytes, begin: bytes, end: bytes) -> bytes:
    require(payload.count(begin) == 1 and payload.count(end) == 1, "marker count mismatch")
    start = payload.index(begin) + len(begin)
    finish = payload.index(end, start)
    require(start <= finish, "marker order mismatch")
    return payload[start:finish]


def file_record(root: Path, path: Path) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
    relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
    info = path.lstat()
    mode = f"{stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode):04o}"
    if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        size = 0
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
        try:
            while True:
                block = os.read(fd, 1024 * 1024)
                if not block:
                    break
                digest.update(block)
                size += len(block)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
        kind = "regular"
        content_sha = digest.hexdigest()
        target = None
        regular_bytes = size
    elif stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):
        target = os.readlink(path)
        encoded = os.fsencode(target)
        kind = "symlink"
        size = len(encoded)
        content_sha = sha(encoded)
        regular_bytes = 0
    elif stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
        target = None
        kind = "directory"
        size = 0
        content_sha = EMPTY_SHA
        regular_bytes = 0
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("unsupported tree entry")
    return compact({
        "mode": mode,
        "path": relative,
        "sha256": content_sha,
        "size": size,
        "symlink_target": target,
        "type": kind,
    }) + b"\n", regular_bytes


def tree_identity(root: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require(root.is_dir() and not root.is_symlink(), "unsafe tree root")
    paths = sorted(root.rglob("*"), key=lambda item: os.fsencode(item.relative_to(root).as_posix()))
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    regular_bytes = 0
    for path in paths:
        row, size = file_record(root, path)
        digest.update(row)
        regular_bytes += size
    return {
        "path_count": len(paths),
        "regular_file_bytes": regular_bytes,
        "sha256": digest.hexdigest(),
    }

DRIVER_PHASE_POLICY = br'''def predecessor_phase(version: str, suffix: str) -> str:
    require(version in {"V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6", "V7", "V8", "V9", "V10", "V11", "V12"}, "unknown predecessor phase version")
    return "M3S_" + version + "_" + suffix


def predecessor_successor_phase(version: str, suffix: str = "") -> str:
    require(version in {"V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6", "V7", "V8", "V9", "V10", "V11", "V12"}, "unknown predecessor successor version")
    return "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version + suffix


def predecessor_dry_run_phase(version: str, suffix: str) -> str:
    require(version in {"V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6", "V7", "V8", "V9", "V10", "V11", "V12"}, "unknown predecessor dry-run version")
    return "M3_SUCCESSOR_DRY_RUN_" + version + "_" + suffix


def versioned_phase_tokens(version: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    require(version in {"V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6", "V7", "V8", "V9", "V10", "V11", "V12", "V13", "V14"}, "unknown phase version")
    return (
        "M3S_" + version + "_SOURCE_WRITE", "M3S_" + version + "_SELF_CHECK",
        "M3S_" + version + "_FINALIZE", "M3S_" + version + "_FINAL_INDEX",
        "M3S_" + version + "_WRITER_SELF_TEST", "M3S_" + version + "_AUTH_HANDOFF",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version,
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version + "_PREFLIGHT",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version + "_FINAL_INDEX",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version + "_TOOLCHAIN_SNAPSHOT",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version + "_READY_FOR_CONTROLLER_REVIEW",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version + "_STOP",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version + "_PRESERVATION",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_" + version + "_STOPPED",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_DRY_RUN_" + version + "_CAPTURE",
        "M3_SUCCESSOR_DRY_RUN_" + version + "_VALIDATION",
    )


def active_v13_phases() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    return versioned_phase_tokens("V13")


def predecessor_active_phases(version: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    require(version in {"V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6", "V7", "V8", "V9", "V10", "V11", "V12"}, "unknown predecessor phase version")
    return versioned_phase_tokens(version)


def exact_python_string_tokens(payload: bytes) -> frozenset[str]:
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(payload, filename="<phase-source-policy>")
    except SyntaxError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError("phase source is not valid Python") from exc
    return frozenset(node.value for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, str))


def phase_source_violations(payload: bytes, require_active: bool) -> list[str]:
    active = active_v13_phases()
    stale = tuple(phase for version in ("V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6", "V7", "V8", "V9", "V10", "V11", "V12") for phase in predecessor_active_phases(version))
    future = versioned_phase_tokens("V14")
    tokens = exact_python_string_tokens(payload)
    violations: list[str] = []
    if require_active:
        violations.extend("missing_active:" + phase for phase in active if phase not in tokens)
    violations.extend("stale_predecessor:" + phase for phase in stale if phase in tokens)
    violations.extend("future_v14:" + phase for phase in future if phase in tokens)
    forbidden = (b"candidate.dygENR4n" + b"/repo", b"--" + b"last", b"resume_liveclip" + b".sh")
    violations.extend("forbidden:" + token.decode("ascii") for token in forbidden if token in payload)
    return violations


def validate_active_phase_names() -> dict[str, Any]:
    payload, identity = read_regular(DRIVER)
    violations = phase_source_violations(payload, True)
    require(violations == [], "successor phase policy violation: " + ",".join(violations))
    active_fixture = b"\n".join(json.dumps(phase).encode("ascii") for phase in active_v13_phases())
    require(phase_source_violations(active_fixture, True) == [], "positive active-phase fixture failed")
    prefix = "M3_SUCCESSOR_PREPARATION_"
    collision_values = (prefix + "V1", prefix + "V10", prefix + "V11", prefix + "V12", prefix + "V13")
    collision_fixture = b"\n".join(json.dumps(phase).encode("ascii") for phase in collision_values)
    require(exact_python_string_tokens(collision_fixture) == frozenset(collision_values), "phase prefix fixture failed")
    for version in ("V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6", "V7", "V8", "V9", "V10", "V11", "V12"):
        stale = predecessor_phase(version, "SELF_CHECK")
        require(phase_source_violations(active_fixture + b"\n" + json.dumps(stale).encode("ascii"), True) == ["stale_predecessor:" + stale], "stale phase fixture failed")
    future = "M3S_" + "V14_SELF_CHECK"
    require(phase_source_violations(active_fixture + b"\n" + json.dumps(future).encode("ascii"), True) == ["future_v14:" + future], "future phase fixture failed")
    return {"active_phases": list(active_v13_phases()), "comparison": "AST_EXACT_STRING_TOKENS", "driver": identity, "violations": violations}


'''

DRIVER_AUTH = br'''class AuthHandoffStop(RuntimeError):
    pass


def auth_stop(code: str) -> None:
    require(re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z0-9_]+", code) is not None, "invalid auth stop code")
    raise AuthHandoffStop(code)


def auth_child_environment(home: Path, tmp: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    env = {
        "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0", "HOME": str(home), "LANG": "C", "LC_ALL": "C",
        "PATH": PATH_VALUE, "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1", "TMPDIR": str(tmp),
        "__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING": CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING,
    }
    require(not any(SECRET_NAME.search(name) for name in env), "credential variable present")
    require("CODEX_HOME" not in env, "CODEX_HOME forbidden")
    return env


def opaque_copy_auth_state(destination: Path) -> tuple[str, int]:
    try:
        before = AUTH_SOURCE.lstat()
        if not (stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode) and not AUTH_SOURCE.is_symlink() and before.st_uid == CURRENT_UID and stat.S_IMODE(before.st_mode) == 0o600 and 0 < before.st_size <= AUTH_MAX_BYTES):
            auth_stop("SOURCE_UNSAFE")
        source_fd = os.open(AUTH_SOURCE, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    except AuthHandoffStop:
        raise
    except BaseException:
        auth_stop("SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE")
    try:
        opened = os.fstat(source_fd)
        source_guard = (opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino, opened.st_uid, stat.S_IMODE(opened.st_mode), opened.st_size, opened.st_mtime_ns, opened.st_ctime_ns)
        expected_guard = (before.st_dev, before.st_ino, before.st_uid, stat.S_IMODE(before.st_mode), before.st_size, before.st_mtime_ns, before.st_ctime_ns)
        if source_guard != expected_guard:
            auth_stop("SOURCE_CHANGED")
        try:
            destination_fd = os.open(destination, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
        except BaseException:
            auth_stop("DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE")
        try:
            while True:
                chunk = os.read(source_fd, 65536)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                view = memoryview(chunk)
                while view:
                    written = os.write(destination_fd, view)
                    if written <= 0:
                        auth_stop("DESTINATION_WRITE_FAILED")
                    view = view[written:]
            os.fsync(destination_fd)
        finally:
            os.close(destination_fd)
        final_source = os.fstat(source_fd)
        after = AUTH_SOURCE.lstat()
        final_guard = (final_source.st_dev, final_source.st_ino, final_source.st_uid, stat.S_IMODE(final_source.st_mode), final_source.st_size, final_source.st_mtime_ns, final_source.st_ctime_ns)
        path_guard = (after.st_dev, after.st_ino, after.st_uid, stat.S_IMODE(after.st_mode), after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns, after.st_ctime_ns)
        if final_guard != source_guard or path_guard != source_guard:
            auth_stop("SOURCE_CHANGED")
    finally:
        os.close(source_fd)
    info = destination.lstat()
    if not (stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and not destination.is_symlink() and info.st_uid == CURRENT_UID and stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) == 0o600):
        auth_stop("DESTINATION_UNSAFE")
    fsync_directory(destination.parent)
    return "0600", info.st_uid


def terminate_auth_process(process: subprocess.Popen[bytes]) -> None:
    try:
        process.terminate()
        process.wait(timeout=5)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            process.kill()
            process.wait(timeout=5)
        except BaseException:
            auth_stop("LOGIN_STATUS_TERMINATION_FAILED")


def codex_login_status(repo: Path, home: Path, tmp: Path) -> str:
    try:
        link = CODEX.lstat()
        if not stat.S_ISLNK(link.st_mode) or Path(os.readlink(CODEX)) != CODEX_TARGET:
            auth_stop("CODEX_IDENTITY_MISMATCH")
        require_identity(CODEX_TARGET, CODEX_SHA, 0o755, CODEX_SIZE)
        process = subprocess.Popen(  # noqa: S603 - exact pinned Codex status argv
            [str(CODEX), "login", "status"], cwd=repo,
            env=auth_child_environment(home, tmp), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            start_new_session=True, shell=False,
        )
        try:
            returncode = process.wait(timeout=30)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            terminate_auth_process(process)
            auth_stop("LOGIN_STATUS_TIMEOUT")
        if returncode != 0:
            auth_stop("LOGIN_STATUS_NOT_AUTHENTICATED")
    except AuthHandoffStop:
        raise
    except BaseException:
        auth_stop("LOGIN_STATUS_FAILED")
    return "SUPPORTED_AUTHENTICATED"


def auth_receipt(copy_success: bool, destination_mode: str | None, destination_owner_uid: int | None, login_status: str, result: str, sanitized_error: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "copy_success": copy_success,
        "destination_mode": destination_mode,
        "destination_owner_uid": destination_owner_uid,
        "format_version": 1,
        "login_status": login_status,
        "phase": "M3S_V13_AUTH_HANDOFF",
        "result": result,
        "sanitized_error": sanitized_error,
    }


def validate_auth_preconditions(values: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[Path, Path, Path]:
    self_identity(values["expected_self_sha"])
    validate_active_phase_names()
    require(Path(values["base"]) == BASE, "base path mismatch")
    validate_documents(values["plan"], values["expected_plan_sha256"], values["status"], values["expected_status_sha256"])
    root = validated_private_directory(M2B)
    del root
    expected_root_receipts = {"source-receipt.json", "writer-self-test.json", "self-check-result.json", "final-index.json", EXECUTION_RESULT_NAME}
    require(set(os.listdir(M2B / "receipts")) == expected_root_receipts, "auth root receipt set mismatch")
    require(not (M2B / "receipts" / AUTH_RESULT_NAME).exists() and not (M2B / "receipts" / AUTH_RESULT_NAME).is_symlink(), "auth result already exists")
    require_identity(M2B / "receipts/final-index.json", values["expected_bootstrap_final_index_sha256"], 0o600)
    execution_identity = require_identity(M2B / "receipts" / EXECUTION_RESULT_NAME, values["expected_execute_result_sha256"], 0o600)
    del execution_identity
    execution, _ = load_json(M2B / "receipts" / EXECUTION_RESULT_NAME)
    require(execution["returncode"] == 0 and execution["timed_out"] is False and execution["output_truncated"] is False and execution["credential_variables"] == [] and execution["wrapper_error"] is None and sha(argv_json(execution["argv"])) == values["expected_execute_argv_json_sha256"], "candidate execution receipt mismatch")
    candidate = Path(values["candidate"])
    require(candidate.parent == BASE and re.fullmatch(r"candidate\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+", candidate.name) is not None and candidate.name not in PREDECESSORS, "candidate path mismatch")
    require(set(path.name for path in BASE.iterdir() if path.name.startswith("candidate.") and path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink()) == set(PREDECESSORS) | {candidate.name}, "postallocation candidate set mismatch")
    candidate_tree, totals = tree_manifest(candidate)
    require(totals["path_count"] == int(values["expected_candidate_tree_path_count"]) and totals["regular_file_bytes"] == int(values["expected_candidate_tree_regular_bytes"]) and sha(candidate_tree) == values["expected_candidate_tree_sha256"], "candidate tree mismatch")
    candidate_receipts = candidate / "successor-receipts"
    require_identity(candidate_receipts / "final-receipt-index.json", values["expected_candidate_final_index_sha256"], 0o600)
    run_id = values["run_id"]
    require(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z-[0-9a-f]{8}", run_id) is not None and run_id != PREVIOUS_M3S_V12_RUN_ID, "run id mismatch")
    run = candidate / "repo/.loop/runs" / run_id
    state = run / "state.json"
    events = run / "events.jsonl"
    state_payload = require_identity(state, values["expected_state_sha256"], 0o644)
    events_payload = require_identity(events, values["expected_events_sha256"], 0o644)
    del state_payload, events_payload
    state_value, _ = load_json(state)
    require(state_value["run_id"] == run_id and state_value["state"] == "received" and state_value["cycle"] == 0 and state_value["code_cycle"] == 0 and state_value["coder_session_id"] is None and state_value["artifacts"] == {} and state_value["command_results"] == [] and state_value["last_error"] is None, "run is not pristine")
    home = candidate / "home"
    tmp = candidate / "tmp"
    private_directory_identity(home)
    private_directory_identity(tmp)
    codex_home = home / ".codex"
    private_directory_identity(codex_home)
    destination = codex_home / "auth.json"
    require(not destination.exists() and not destination.is_symlink(), "auth destination already exists")
    return candidate / "repo", home, tmp


def auth_handoff(values: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    result_path = M2B / "receipts" / AUTH_RESULT_NAME
    copy_success = False
    destination_mode: str | None = None
    destination_owner_uid: int | None = None
    login_status = "NOT_RUN"
    try:
        repo, home, tmp = validate_auth_preconditions(values)
        destination = home / ".codex/auth.json"
        destination_mode, destination_owner_uid = opaque_copy_auth_state(destination)
        copy_success = True
        login_status = codex_login_status(repo, home, tmp)
        receipt = auth_receipt(True, destination_mode, destination_owner_uid, login_status, "READY_FOR_CONTROLLER_REVIEW", None)
        write_exclusive(result_path, pretty(receipt))
        os.write(1, compact(receipt) + b"\n")
        return 0
    except AuthHandoffStop as exc:
        receipt = auth_receipt(copy_success, destination_mode, destination_owner_uid, login_status, "STOPPED", str(exc))
    except BaseException:
        receipt = auth_receipt(copy_success, destination_mode, destination_owner_uid, login_status, "STOPPED", "UNEXPECTED_STOP")
    try:
        write_exclusive(result_path, pretty(receipt))
    except BaseException:
        return 1
    os.write(1, compact(receipt) + b"\n")
    return 1


'''


def replace_once(payload: bytes, old: bytes, new: bytes, label: str) -> bytes:
    require(payload.count(old) == 1, label + " replacement count mismatch")
    return payload.replace(old, new, 1)


def derive_driver(source: bytes) -> bytes:
    require(len(source) == V12_DRIVER_SIZE and sha(source) == V12_DRIVER_SHA, "V12 driver identity mismatch")
    require(source.count(b"V12") == 52 and source.count(b"v12") == 53, "V12 token count mismatch")
    payload = source.replace(b"V12", b"V13").replace(b"v12", b"v13")
    shape_start = payload.index(b"SHAPES = {")
    shape_end = payload.index(b"\n}\n\nPREDECESSORS = {", shape_start) + 2
    payload = payload[:shape_start] + DRIVER_SHAPES + payload[shape_end:]
    payload = replace_once(
        payload,
        b"\n}\n\nPROFILES = {",
        b'    "candidate.mRMO7MQ6": (44416, 949533329, "da0bee90afca60e9861b9052e4c88dfae0ec78015cb30c3f16f571bd144080cb", "92cb4555c3dc2b5738db348c8295cb0583430df764bb2a01942b897e9f8fdc96"),\n}\n\nPROFILES = {',
        "predecessor",
    )
    payload = replace_once(payload, b"OPERATOR_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES = 1024 * 1024\n", DRIVER_V12_CONSTANTS + b"OPERATOR_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES = 1024 * 1024\n", "V12 constants")
    phase_start = payload.index(b"def predecessor_phase(")
    generic_start = payload.index(b"GENERIC_DIRECTORY_KEYS =", phase_start)
    exact_start = payload.index(b"def exact_python_string_tokens", generic_start)
    phase_end = payload.index(b"def validate_stopped_root(", exact_start)
    identity_helpers = payload[generic_start:exact_start]
    phase_policy = replace_once(
        DRIVER_PHASE_POLICY,
        b"def exact_python_string_tokens",
        identity_helpers + b"def exact_python_string_tokens",
        "phase identity helper insertion",
    )
    payload = payload[:phase_start] + phase_policy + payload[phase_end:]
    payload = replace_once(payload, b"def validate_documents(\n", DRIVER_V12_VALIDATOR + b"def validate_documents(\n", "V12 validator")
    payload = replace_once(payload, b'        "m3s_v11_stopped": validate_m3s_v11_stopped(),\n', b'        "m3s_v11_stopped": validate_m3s_v11_stopped(),\n        "m3s_v12_consumed": validate_m3s_v12_consumed(),\n', "V12 gate")
    payload = replace_once(payload, b"    for path in paths:\n        raw = os.fsencode(path.relative_to(root).as_posix())\n", b'    for path in paths:\n        relative_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n        require(relative_path != "home/.codex/auth.json", "credential path excluded from manifests")\n        raw = os.fsencode(relative_path)\n', "manifest auth exclusion")
    old_index = b'''    for key in (
        "transport_argv_json_sha256",
        "self_check_argv_json_sha256",
        "finalize_argv_json_sha256",
    ):
        require(index[key] == values["expected_" + key], key + " mismatch")
'''
    new_index = b'''    require(index["root_prepare_argv_json_sha256"] == values["expected_root_prepare_argv_json_sha256"], "root prepare argv hash mismatch")
'''
    payload = replace_once(payload, old_index, new_index, "root index schema")
    payload = replace_once(payload, b"def execute(values: dict[str, str]) -> int:\n", DRIVER_AUTH + b"def execute(values: dict[str, str]) -> int:\n", "auth implementation")
    old_main = b'''def main() -> int:
    command, values = parse_shape(sys.argv[1:])
    if command == "self-check":
        return self_check(values)
    if command == "finalize":
        return finalize(values)
    return execute(values)
'''
    new_main = b'''def main() -> int:
    command, values = parse_shape(sys.argv[1:])
    if command == "auth-handoff":
        return auth_handoff(values)
    return execute(values)
'''
    payload = replace_once(payload, old_main, new_main, "main dispatch")
    return payload


def function_node(tree: ast.Module, name: str) -> ast.FunctionDef:
    node = next((item for item in tree.body if isinstance(item, ast.FunctionDef) and item.name == name), None)
    require(isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef), "missing function: " + name)
    return node


def validate_derived_driver(payload: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]:
    tree = ast.parse(payload, filename="<m3s-v13-derived-driver>")
    compile(tree, "<m3s-v13-derived-driver>", "exec", dont_inherit=True)
    functions = {item.name for item in tree.body if isinstance(item, ast.FunctionDef)}
    required = {"execute", "auth_handoff", "opaque_copy_auth_state", "codex_login_status", "validate_m3s_v12_consumed", "seal_attempt", "initialize_and_bind_successor"}
    require(required <= functions, "derived driver function set mismatch")
    constants = {item.targets[0].id: item.value for item in tree.body if isinstance(item, ast.Assign) and len(item.targets) == 1 and isinstance(item.targets[0], ast.Name)}
    shapes = ast.literal_eval(constants["SHAPES"])
    require(set(shapes) == {"execute", "auth-handoff"}, "derived driver command set mismatch")
    predecessors = ast.literal_eval(constants["PREDECESSORS"])
    require(len(predecessors) == 17 and "candidate.mRMO7MQ6" in predecessors, "derived predecessor set mismatch")
    copy_node = function_node(tree, "opaque_copy_auth_state")
    forbidden_copy_calls = {"compact", "hash_regular", "json", "pretty", "read_regular", "require_identity", "sha"}
    for call in (node for node in ast.walk(copy_node) if isinstance(node, ast.Call)):
        if isinstance(call.func, ast.Name):
            require(call.func.id not in forbidden_copy_calls, "auth copy inspects or serializes credential bytes")
        if isinstance(call.func, ast.Attribute):
            require(call.func.attr not in {"read_bytes", "read_text", "hexdigest", "digest"}, "auth copy hashes or decodes credential bytes")
    require(not any(isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name) and node.func.value.id == "os" and node.func.attr in {"unlink", "remove", "rename", "replace"} for node in ast.walk(copy_node)), "auth copy has destructive path")
    status_node = function_node(tree, "codex_login_status")
    popen = [node for node in ast.walk(status_node) if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name) and node.func.value.id == "subprocess" and node.func.attr == "Popen"]
    require(len(popen) == 1, "login status Popen count mismatch")
    rendered = ast.unparse(popen[0])
    require("['/opt/homebrew/bin/codex', 'login', 'status']" in rendered or "[str(CODEX), 'login', 'status']" in rendered, "login status argv mismatch")
    require("stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL" in rendered and "stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL" in rendered and "shell=False" in rendered, "login status channel policy mismatch")
    require(payload.count(b'["/usr/bin/mktemp", "-d", str(BASE / "candidate.XXXXXXXX")]') == 1, "mktemp site mismatch")
    require(payload.count(b'        "loop-init",\n') == 1, "loop-init site mismatch")
    require(b"--last" not in payload and b"resume_liveclip.sh" not in payload, "forbidden resume token")
    require(payload.count(b'"home/.codex/auth.json"') == 1, "manifest exclusion count mismatch")
    return {
        "auth_copy_no_hash_parse_serialize": True,
        "command_set": sorted(shapes),
        "compile_only": "PASS",
        "function_count": len(functions),
        "login_status_channels": "DEVNULL",
        "mktemp_sites": 1,
        "predecessor_count": len(predecessors),
        "result": "PASS",
    }


def git_output(argv: list[str]) -> bytes:
    env = {
        "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0", "HOME": "/Users/junhuaxu", "LANG": "C",
        "LC_ALL": "C", "PATH": PATH_VALUE, "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1",
        "TMPDIR": "/tmp",  # noqa: S108 - fixed zero-write pre-root environment
        "__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING": CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING,
    }
    result = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - exact read-only Git argv from trusted code
        argv, cwd=DELIVERY, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, check=False, timeout=30,
    )
    require(result.returncode == 0 and len(result.stdout) <= 1024 * 1024 and len(result.stderr) <= 65536, "git preflight failed")
    return result.stdout


def validate_inventory() -> dict[str, Any]:
    require(git_output(["/usr/bin/git", "branch", "--show-current"]) == (EXPECTED_BRANCH + "\n").encode(), "branch mismatch")
    require(git_output(["/usr/bin/git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"]) == (EXPECTED_HEAD + "\n").encode(), "HEAD mismatch")
    lines = git_output(["/usr/bin/git", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=all"]).decode().splitlines()
    counts = (
        sum(1 for line in lines if line[:1] not in {" ", "?"}),
        sum(1 for line in lines if len(line) > 1 and line[1] not in {" ", "?"}),
        sum(1 for line in lines if line.startswith("??")),
    )
    require(counts == (EXPECTED_STAGED, EXPECTED_MODIFIED, EXPECTED_UNTRACKED), "inventory mismatch")
    candidates = {path.name for path in BASE.iterdir() if path.name.startswith("candidate.") and path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink()}
    require(candidates == EXPECTED_CANDIDATES, "candidate set mismatch")
    return {"branch": EXPECTED_BRANCH, "candidate_count": len(candidates), "head": EXPECTED_HEAD, "status_counts": counts}


def validate_v12_evidence() -> dict[str, Any]:
    private_directory(V12_ROOT, {"candidate-driver.py", "home", "tmp", "receipts"})
    private_directory(V12_ROOT / "home", set())
    private_directory(V12_ROOT / "tmp", set())
    private_directory(V12_ROOT / "receipts", {"source-receipt.json", "writer-self-test.json", "self-check-result.json", "final-index.json", "successor-preparation-v12-result.json"})
    files = {name: identity(V12_ROOT / name, size, digest, 0o600) for name, (size, digest) in V12_ROOT_FILES.items()}
    state = identity(V12_RUN / "state.json", *V12_STATE, 0o644)
    events = identity(V12_RUN / "events.jsonl", *V12_EVENTS, 0o644)
    planner = identity(V12_RUN / "agents/planner/001-events.jsonl", *V12_PLANNER_EVENTS, 0o644)
    value = json.loads(read_regular(V12_RUN / "state.json")[0].decode())
    require(value["run_id"] == "20261009T235710Z-7716e9ad" and value["state"] == "blocked" and value["cycle"] == 1 and value["code_cycle"] == 0 and value["coder_session_id"] is None and value["artifacts"] == {} and value["command_results"] == [], "V12 terminal state mismatch")
    tree = tree_identity(V12_CANDIDATE)
    require(tree == {"path_count": V12_CANDIDATE_PATHS, "regular_file_bytes": V12_CANDIDATE_BYTES, "sha256": V12_CANDIDATE_SHA}, "V12 candidate tree mismatch")
    return {"candidate_tree": tree, "files": files, "terminal": {"events": events, "planner_events": planner, "state": state}}


def write_exclusive(path: Path, payload: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]:
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
    try:
        view = memoryview(payload)
        while view:
            written = os.write(fd, view)
            require(written > 0, "zero write")
            view = view[written:]
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    observed, info = read_regular(path)
    require(observed == payload and stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) == 0o600, "exclusive write mismatch")
    return {"mode": "0600", "sha256": sha(payload), "size": len(payload)}


def fsync_directory(path: Path) -> None:
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    try:
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    require(sys.argv[0] == "-c" and sys.argv[1:2] == ["--"], "literal -c source required")
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(allow_abbrev=False)
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("root-only",))
    parser.add_argument("--plan", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-plan-sha256", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--status", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-status-sha256", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-source-size", required=True, type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-source-sha256", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-driver-size", required=True, type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-driver-sha256", required=True)
    return parser.parse_args(sys.argv[2:])


def validate_environment() -> None:
    expected = {
        "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0", "HOME": "/Users/junhuaxu", "LANG": "C",
        "LC_ALL": "C", "PATH": PATH_VALUE, "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1",
        "TMPDIR": "/tmp",  # noqa: S108 - fixed zero-write pre-root environment
        "__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING": CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING,
    }
    require(dict(os.environ) == expected and os.getuid() == CURRENT_UID and Path.cwd() == SEED, "root environment mismatch")


def root_only(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    validate_environment()
    require(Path(args.plan) == PLAN and Path(args.status) == STATUS, "document path mismatch")
    require(not ROOT.exists() and not ROOT.is_symlink(), "V13 root already exists")
    plan_bytes, _ = read_regular(PLAN, LIVING_PLAN_MAX_BYTES)
    status_bytes, _ = read_regular(STATUS)
    require(sha(plan_bytes) == args.expected_plan_sha256 and sha(status_bytes) == args.expected_status_sha256, "document hash mismatch")
    source = extract_once(plan_bytes, SOURCE_BEGIN, SOURCE_END)
    require((len(source), sha(source)) == (args.expected_source_size, args.expected_source_sha256), "preparation source identity mismatch")
    v12_driver, _ = read_regular(V12_DRIVER)
    derived = derive_driver(v12_driver)
    require((len(derived), sha(derived)) == (args.expected_driver_size, args.expected_driver_sha256), "derived driver identity mismatch")
    static = validate_derived_driver(derived)
    repeat = derive_driver(v12_driver)
    require(repeat == derived, "driver derivation is not deterministic")
    inventory = validate_inventory()
    v12 = validate_v12_evidence()
    require(not ROOT.exists() and not ROOT.is_symlink(), "V13 root appeared during preflight")
    root_argv_sha = sha(argv_json([str(PYTHON), "-c", source.decode("utf-8"), *sys.argv[1:]]))
    os.mkdir(ROOT, 0o700)
    fsync_directory(ROOT.parent)
    for name in ("home", "tmp", "receipts"):
        os.mkdir(ROOT / name, 0o700)
        fsync_directory(ROOT)
    driver_identity = write_exclusive(DRIVER, derived)
    source_receipt = write_exclusive(RECEIPTS / "source-receipt.json", pretty({
        "documents": {"plan_sha256": args.expected_plan_sha256, "status_sha256": args.expected_status_sha256},
        "driver": driver_identity, "format_version": 1, "phase": "M3S_V13_SOURCE_WRITE",
        "preparation_source": {"sha256": args.expected_source_sha256, "size": args.expected_source_size},
        "result": "PASS", "root_prepare_argv_json_sha256": root_argv_sha,
    }))
    writer_test = write_exclusive(RECEIPTS / "writer-self-test.json", pretty({
        "deterministic_derivation": True, "format_version": 1,
        "no_replace_driver_write": True, "phase": "M3S_V13_WRITER_SELF_TEST",
        "result": "PASS",
    }))
    self_check = write_exclusive(RECEIPTS / "self-check-result.json", pretty({
        "format_version": 1, "phase": "M3S_V13_SELF_CHECK", "result": "PASS",
        "static": static, "v12_terminal_evidence": v12["terminal"],
    }))
    final_payload = pretty({
        "documents": {"plan_sha256": args.expected_plan_sha256, "status_sha256": args.expected_status_sha256},
        "driver": driver_identity, "files": {"source-receipt.json": source_receipt, "writer-self-test.json": writer_test, "self-check-result.json": self_check},
